name: settings-pane-header-drags-the-window
description:
The settings window has no native titlebar, and until now its only drag handle was the 40px .settings-drag-region strip above the sidebar - a press anywhere else on the window's own background, including the pane header row beside the pane title or the sidebar's own empty space, started a text selection instead of moving the window. settings.css now marks the pane heading and the sidebar background as drag regions, with every control, row, scroll container (.settings-rail, .settings-search-results) and a few plain-div pointer targets (the glass-opacity slider track, an engine/routing row, the theme studio canvas) punching their own hole back out. The pane content itself is deliberately NOT a drag region: on macOS a wheel over a drag region never reaches the page (AppKit picks the wheel target with the hitTest: that returns nil for HTCAPTION), so a drag rule on the whole pane stalled the scroll everywhere but over a control. The heading is a block, so a press beside its text still moves the window.

This measures the part the node suite cannot: dom-shim has no layout engine, so it can assert the CSS rule text and that a real element matches the no-drag selector list, but not that an actual mouse press at a real point on screen moves a real OS window. That is what this scenario drives, with a real cgevent drag rather than move_window's own AX call - AX would move the window on its own regardless of whether the fix works, which would make the assertion pass either way. Two drags run, from two different backgrounds - the pane content and the sidebar - since each is its own drag region in the CSS and a fix to one does not prove the other.

axresize (move_window/resize/get) always targets the LARGEST AX window of the app, not the frontmost one, so the browser window is shrunk to 700x500 before Settings opens - otherwise move_window would reposition the browser window behind it instead. move_window puts Settings at a known screen position before each drag, so its start and end points can be aimed in absolute screen coordinates: the pane point (40+650, 50+35) is computed from the layout (a 190px sidebar column, the pane's own 24px/26px padding, a 20px heading) and sits well clear of both the heading text and the pane's right edge; the sidebar point (40+3, 50+46) sits in the search field's own wrap padding, left of the field and above the rail. Both points are gated by their own elementFromPoint check before the real drag runs.

actions.note: gate: the startup tab committed, so the app is up
Atrium frontmost, so the chord reaches it
the browser window - only one window exists yet, so this cannot land anywhere else. Shrinks it under Settings' own 860x620 default, or the next move_window would target this window instead
open Settings; its menu item is not reachable from a scenario
window opens on General at 860x620 - now the largest AX window, so it is the one axresize reaches below
a known screen position, so the drag below can be aimed in absolute coordinates rather than wherever CenterWindow happened to land it

actions.expression: (() => { const el = document.elementFromPoint(650, 35); if (!el) return 'nothing-there'; if (el.closest('.settings-drag-region')) return 'on-old-strip'; return (el.closest('.settings-pane-content') && !el.closest('button, input, select, textarea')) ? 'on-pane-background' : 'unexpected: ' + el.className; })()
actions.note: gates the scenario's own setup - 650,35 has to land beside the General heading, past the old strip and off every control, or the drag below would prove nothing

actions.expression: (() => { const r = (s) => getComputedStyle(document.querySelector(s)).webkitAppRegion || getComputedStyle(document.querySelector(s)).appRegion; return 'heading=' + r('.settings-heading') + ' pane=' + r('.settings-pane-content'); })()
actions.note: the deployed CSS, as the renderer resolved it: the heading is the drag handle, and the pane content is not - a wheel over a drag region never reaches the page on macOS, so this line is the scroll bug's regression guard

actions.expression: (() => { window.__dragStart = {x: window.screenX, y: window.screenY}; return true; })()
actions.note: screenX/screenY read the window's real position from the renderer - stashed here so the after-drag eval can diff against it without a second round trip

THE MEASUREMENT (pane): a real cgevent mouse drag from the pane background (40+650, 50+35) rightward by 60. Horizontal, like every other drag action in this suite - a first diagonal attempt moved the window in x by the full delta and not at all in y, which is AppKit's native window-drag loop under a synthetic gesture, not this fix. No expect_width - that correction loop only understands the sidebar resize grip's own vlog line, not a window move
a real cgevent drag lands short by a different amount each run, so this checks against the 60 asked for within a loose tolerance rather than an exact match

actions.expression: (() => { const b = window.__dragStart; return 'before ' + b.x + ',' + b.y + ' after ' + window.screenX + ',' + window.screenY; })()
actions.note: recorded: the numbers behind moved-right-pane, including y for evidence even though nothing asserts on it
the window at its new position after the pane drag
reset to the same known position for the second drag below - the pane drag above already moved the window, and the sidebar drag's own screen coordinates are computed from this exact origin

actions.expression: (() => { const el = document.elementFromPoint(3, 46); if (!el) return 'nothing-there'; if (el.closest('.settings-drag-region')) return 'on-old-strip'; if (el.closest('.settings-rail')) return 'on-rail'; return (el.closest('.settings-sidebar') && !el.closest('button, input, select, textarea')) ? 'on-sidebar-background' : 'unexpected: ' + el.className; })()
actions.note: gates the second drag - 3,46 sits in the search wrap's own padding (past the 40px strip, left of the field, above the rail), not on the rail or the old strip

actions.expression: (() => { window.__dragStart = {x: window.screenX, y: window.screenY}; return true; })()
actions.note: re-stashed against the position after the reset move_window above, not the pane drag's own result
THE MEASUREMENT (sidebar): a real cgevent mouse drag from the sidebar background (40+3, 50+46) rightward by 40 - a point in the sidebar column, off the rail and off the old strip
same loose tolerance as moved-right-pane, against the 40 asked for here

actions.expression: (() => { const b = window.__dragStart; return 'before ' + b.x + ',' + b.y + ' after ' + window.screenX + ',' + window.screenY; })()
actions.note: recorded: the numbers behind moved-right-sidebar
the window at its new position after the sidebar drag

assertions.note: the browser window and the settings window
